samples.summary: New docs `setImageUrlResolver` seam has no test at all, unlike every sibling engine
samples.evidence: The diff adds a module-level `urlResolver` and `setImageUrlResolver` to packages/docs/src/view/image-cache.ts, and `getOrLoadImage` now fetches/caches under `urlResolver(logicalSrc)`. Grepping packages/docs for `setImageUrlResolver|getOrLoadImage|image-cache` finds only source files (index.ts, doc-canvas.ts, paint-layout.ts, table-renderer.ts) — no test file. The three engines this deliberately mirrors each pin the seam: packages/slides/test/view/canvas/image-cache-resolver.test.ts (5 cases: resolved URL is fetched, identity by default, `null` restores identity, cache/eviction keyed by the resolved URL), packages/notes/src/view/preview-image-resolver.test.ts, packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/image-cache.test.ts. So nothing fails if docs' resolver is never applied, is applied to the wrong string, or if the cache keys on the logical src while the fetch uses the resolved one — the exact failure mode is 'shared-link images silently never render', which is the bug this PR exists to fix (#1037). Also untested: the cache is module-global and holds entries keyed by a previously-resolved URL, so a resolver installed/cleared between mounts (StrictMode mount→cleanup→remount) has no coverage.
searchedFor: grep setImageUrlResolver across packages to compare sibling test files

samples.summary: The new `["doc", setDocsImageUrlResolver]` installer entry and the `token`→uploader wiring in SharedDocsLayout are untested
samples.evidence: shared-document.tsx now (a) registers the docs resolver in IMAGE_RESOLVER_INSTALLERS and (b) builds `uploadImage` from `token` and threads it into DocsFormattingToolbar/DocsView. Grep for `IMAGE_RESOLVER_INSTALLERS` finds only shared-document.tsx and no test; the only test under packages/frontend/src/app/shared/__tests__ is shared-blob-routing.test.ts. If the entry or the token thread is dropped, share-link images 403 for everyone including the author and the toolbar silently falls back to the 401-ing owner uploader, with no test failing. Contained to a mis-wire that the (also untested) siblings already share, hence minor.

samples.summary: `failureText` only covered for the happy JSON-with-string-message shape; non-JSON and array-message fallbacks untested
samples.evidence: image-insert.test.ts:83 exercises exactly one body (`{"message":"This share link is read-only","statusCode":403}`). The `catch`/fall-through branch (plain-text body, e.g. a proxy's HTML 413 or Nest's `message: string[]` validation shape, where the code must fall back to the raw body) has no test — a regression there would show the user an empty or `[object Object]` toast. Also untested: `credentials: "include"` on the unauthenticated branch (images.ts:120) — the test asserts only `init?.method`.

samples.summary: No test that `insertImageFromFile` still uses the authenticated owner uploader when `upload` is omitted
samples.evidence: The signature gained a defaulted 4th parameter (`upload: DocsImageUpload = uploadImageFile`). All three tests in the `insertImageFromFile` describe pass an explicit `upload`, so the default binding is never exercised; if the default were changed or dropped the owner (non-shared) image insert would break with the suite still green. The test named "uses the passed uploader rather than the owner default" is also near-vacuous on its second assertion — `fetchWithAuth` cannot be called when an uploader is injected, so `expect(fetchWithAuth).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` holds regardless of the behavior under test.

samples.summary: The credential is untested on the `rawRequest` paths (pinned-through-proxy hop and opaque-redirect fallback)
samples.evidence: The diff changed `issue()` so both `rawRequest(plan.url, plan.agent, headers)` call sites (image-fetcher.ts:848 and :863) now receive the merged `headers` instead of `plan.headers`. The new `describe('createImageFetcher authorization')` block in packages/cli/test/image-fetcher.test.ts drives everything through the injected `fetch` stub only, so neither raw path is covered: nothing fails if the merge dropped the credential (workspace images 401 and vanish from the export) or, conversely, if the credential were forwarded on a raw proxied hop to a non-server origin. Also untested: a same-origin redirect (credential must be *kept* on hop 2) — only the off-origin drop is asserted.
searchedFor: read the new authorization describe block in the diff

samples.summary: Extracted `authorizationHeader` has no direct test, and neither export command's wiring of it is covered
samples.evidence: `authorizationHeader` is newly exported and consumed by commands/docs.ts:341 and commands/slides.ts:235. Grep across packages/cli finds no test importing it; its three branches are only indirectly covered via existing HttpClient tests (packages/cli/test/http-client.test.ts asserts Bearer headers), and no test asserts that `docs export` / `slides export` pass `authorization` into `createImageFetcher` — dropping that argument would silently reintroduce the 401-dropped-image behavior. Low blast radius (export-time only, loud-ish), hence nit.

samples.summary: The new 30/min `@Throttle` and the HTTP status/message of the authorization refusals are not asserted
samples.evidence: image-share-upload.controller.spec.ts asserts Forbidden/BadRequest at the unit level (direct `ctrl.upload` calls) and multipart bounds over HTTP, but the HTTP suite registers no ThrottlerGuard, so the deliberately-lowered `limit: 30` is unverified, and no HTTP case pins 403 + the user-facing wording (`This share link is read-only`) that the frontend's `failureText` surfaces. Sibling controllers (images/image-read/files) likewise have no throttle test, so this matches existing practice — nit rather than a gap.

verdict.reason: Verified the seam exists and is untested. packages/docs/src/view/image-cache.ts:33-44 adds module-level `urlResolver` + `setImageUrlResolver`, and getOrLoadImage:57 resolves the src before using it as both fetch URL and cache key; it is exported at packages/docs/src/index.ts:211 and installed by packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:49. Repo-wide greps for `setImageUrlResolver|getOrLoadImage|image-cache|urlResolver` (both pages of results) show every docs-package hit is a source file; no test file in the repo imports docs' seam. packages/docs has no colocated tests (glob packages/docs/src/**/*.test.ts -> none) and packages/docs/test/ has zero hits for image-cache/getOrLoadImage, nor any resolver/token test relating to images. Indirect coverage was ruled out: the three call sites (doc-canvas, paint-layout, table-renderer) do have tests, but since setImageUrlResolver is never invoked in any test, none can fail if the resolver is not applied, is applied to the wrong string, or if the cache keys the logical src while the fetch uses the resolved URL. Adjacent share-link tests cover different units (image-insert.test.ts upload route; share-image-url.test.ts URL builder; shared-blob-routing.test.ts sharedBlobKind). Sibling engines each pin the seam (slides image-cache-resolver.test.ts:48-84, notes preview-image-resolver.test.ts:23-80, sheets image-cache.test.ts:44-83), confirming the asymmetry. Major: the untested behavior is the shared-link image render path the change exists to fix, so a regression ships as 'images silently never render' for anonymous viewers.

finding.summary: The new unauthenticated upload route's Multer `fileFilter` (MIME allowlist) and `fileSize` limit are never exercised by its spec
finding.evidence: `image-share-upload.controller.spec.ts` constructs the controller directly (`new ApiV1ShareImageUploadController(...)`) and calls `ctrl.upload(pngFile(), 'tok')`, so the `@UseInterceptors(FileInterceptor(...))` config — `limits.fileSize: IMAGE_UPLOAD_MULTER_LIMIT_BYTES` and the `ALLOWED_IMAGE_MIME_TYPES` `fileFilter` with `unsupportedFileTypeMessage` — is inert metadata during the test. `pngFile()`'s `mimetype: 'image/png'` is decorative: an `image/svg+xml` or over-cap body would take the exact same code path in this spec. The sibling upload route pins both through supertest (`images.controller.spec.ts:65-105`: 413 on `cap + 1024`, 400 with `Unsupported file type: image/svg+xml`). Since this is the only *unauthenticated* write in the image module, a wrong constant or an omitted filter would ship undetected as arbitrary-type / unbounded-size anonymous upload.

verdict.reason: The spec file the finding names already exercises both Multer bounds over real HTTP. Besides the direct-construction unit tests (lines 39-116, which the finding describes accurately), image-share-upload.controller.spec.ts contains a second describe block, 'POST /api/v1/shared/images (multipart bounds)' (lines 129-245), which compiles a testing module with ApiV1ShareImageUploadController and calls createNestApplication()/app.init() (lines 136-146), then drives the route with supertest so the @UseInterceptors(FileInterceptor(...)) config actually runs. It pins limits.fileSize on both sides of the boundary: 201 for a body of exactly cap (161-175) and 413 with message 'File too large' plus upload not called for Buffer.alloc(cap + 1024) (177-192). It pins the fileFilter allowlist: 400 with the hard-coded literal 'Unsupported file type: image/svg+xml' and upload not called (194-211), a positive loop over all four allowlisted MIME types expecting 201 (213-228), and a case showing the filter refuses before assertCanWrite so findByToken is never called (230-244). The 400 message is deliberately written out rather than derived from unsupportedFileTypeMessage, so it would catch wording/constant drift, and the exact-cap vs cap+1024 pair would catch a wrong IMAGE_UPLOAD_MULTER_LIMIT_BYTES (image.constants.ts:33). This is precisely the supertest parity with images.controller.spec.ts that the finding says is absent, so the absence claim fails.
